test:postgres-real.note: The runner was rebuilt and no longer ships the PostgreSQL 18 binaries the previous receipt named. A fresh PostgreSQL 16.13 cluster was initialized locally for this gate. Recorded as 16.13 rather than carrying the old version forward, because the version is part of what the evidence means. Observed once at 177/178 while three suites were deliberately pointed at one shared long-lived database: "two concurrent recovery workers ... converge on exactly one outcome" failed with neither worker claiming its row. Root cause is cross-test interference, not a source defect -- three test files sweep the shared omnia_v9_external_effect_executions table with broad limits (1000, 500, 50) and node --test runs files in parallel, so another file's sweep can claim this test's row first. FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED makes the "both claimed" branch impossible, so the failure can only be "neither". The suite's documented convention is a disposable per-run database; under it the gate is 178/178, and the same contention on unmodified main also passed. No changed module in this shift appears anywhere in that test's 12-module import graph.

test:mutation-war.note: Run with both a real PostgreSQL and a real Chromium so STORE-01, MONEY-17 and CRAWL-01 execute rather than skip; nothing was skipped in this run. The ten new NORM-*/GENOME-04/GENOME-05 mutations cover body-to-capability normalization and the narrowed instruction scanner. Without them the war reports SKIPPED_NEEDS_POSTGRES / SKIPPED_NEEDS_BROWSER rather than counting them as killed. Verdicts are now read from what each run reports rather than from its exit status: a suite that never ran is SUITE_DID_NOT_RUN, not KILLED, and a green run that asserted nothing is NO_ASSERTIONS_RAN, not SURVIVED.

test:browser.note: This gate caught a P0 this shift: the browser runtime pool integration moved the crawl result variables inside a try block while the return stayed outside it, so every crawl threw ReferenceError. check:syntax parsed it, the deterministic suite does not cover it, and the pool unit tests mock the browser. Only this gate saw it.
